metadata.title: Investigating the sources of teacher intercultural self-efficacy: A three-level study using TALIS 2018

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses TALIS 2018 teacher survey data with a stratified sampling design. To account for unequal selection probability and response rate, the authors include the teacher-level final weight (after adjusting teacher base weight, response rate, and school-level weight) in their multilevel analyses. The paper does not report a replicate-weight scheme (e.g., BRR/jackknife), and it does not indicate that weights were omitted; instead, weights are explicitly used to reflect the complex survey design. No additional outlier trimming or grade/task filtering is described beyond the preregistered sample inclusion criteria (teachers in lower/upper secondary schools with relevant experience and item responses).

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The dependent variable is teacher intercultural self-efficacy measured via TALIS Likert-scale items and modeled via multilevel factor-score/measurement procedures, not via PV-based cognitive achievement scales. Therefore, Plausible Values handling is not applicable in this analysis context. For missing data, the authors explicitly use Full information maximum likelihood (FIML) in Mplus, which is treated here as multiple-imputation-style handling per the provided mapping rules.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: From the TALIS 2018 teacher survey, the authors included only teachers who (1) answered YES to having previously taught a classroom with students from different cultures, (2) answered YES to the current school including students of more than one cultural or ethnic background, and (3) provided responses for any of the intercultural self-efficacy items. They further restricted the sample to teachers working in lower and upper secondary schools. The final analytic sample comprised 91,768 teachers from 11,523 schools across 46 countries (excluding Russia because intercultural self-efficacy was not included in the TALIS questionnaire for Russia).

The outcome is teacher intercultural self-efficacy measured with TALIS Likert-scale items about coping with multicultural classrooms and related classroom practices. The authors use teacher final survey weights to address TALIS’s stratified sampling design and handle missingness with FIML in Mplus. They report that intercultural self-efficacy varies significantly across schools and countries (ICC1: 0.046 for schools; 0.157 for countries). In the multilevel models, intercultural professional development and teacher mobility are positively associated with intercultural self-efficacy, while multicultural climate at the school level is also positive (small effect), and multicultural education policy at the country level is negatively associated (moderate effect) but not robust in robustness checks with listwise deletion. data.null_fields_interpretation: The paper is an empirical multilevel modeling study of teacher self-efficacy using TALIS 2018 and MIPEX indicators, but it does not train or compare machine learning predictive models (no ML algorithms are reported). Therefore, the ML technique fields are intentionally empty and main_findings are not populated under the ML-prediction schema. The results are reported as multilevel regression associations and variance partitioning rather than ML performance metrics.
